deviations.what: Serialize package dispatch to one package per codex actor at a time: wave 0 runs as two rounds (round 1: P1->codex-thor, P2->codex-orin; round 2: P3->codex-thor, P4->codex-orin) instead of four concurrent packages. Waves 1-3 follow the same one-per-actor rule until t16 lands. Task content, acceptance criteria and coverage targets are unchanged — this is a scheduling amendment only.
deviations.reason: Each codex bridge allowlists exactly ONE checkout per host, exact-match — verified live: thor's codex-bridge.json has repo_allowlist=['/home/thor/git/culture-nodes-agent'] and config.py resolves membership by equality. Two concurrent packages on one actor would therefore put two agent sessions in one checkout, which is precisely the concurrent-writer corruption mode spec claim c42 describes, with the c49 fence not yet built (it is task t10). Running it would reproduce, while building the fix, the exact hazard the batch exists to remove. Serializing costs wall-clock and nothing else; t16 (the workspace provisioner, already scheduled in wave 1) restores parallelism for waves 2-3, and this incident is empirical evidence for t16's value rather than an argument for it.

deviations.what: Refresh both codex hosts' allowlisted checkouts to main before dispatching any package.
deviations.reason: thor's /home/thor/git/culture-nodes-agent is at fadfa1d, two commits behind main 7519d74 — so an agent would build against stale code and its diff would not apply cleanly at merge. Observed at wave-0 dispatch; orin unchecked and assumed equally stale until verified.

deviations.what: Commit and push the spec, the plan, the devague frame/plan/delivery state and scripts/verify-token-scope.sh to a branch, and have every subsequent work-package brief reference them via 'git fetch origin && git show origin/<branch>:<path>' instead of inlining the task text into the instruction string.
deviations.reason: Discovered at wave-0 dispatch: run 01M022BSJ3550RQ8Q2P7DFWA91 refused to start because 'docs/plans/2026-08-15-own-the-work-end-to-end.md is absent from this checkout and all local Git refs'. The plan was uncommitted on spark, so the brief referenced a path that does not exist on thor — the same class of defect #74 documents, committed by the operator while dispatching its fix. The workaround (inline every task's full text into the instruction string) does not scale past a two-task package and makes the ledger see one opaque blob instead of citable documents. Committing and pushing costs one branch and fixes the class for every remaining package. The operator approved a cheap in-flight fix via /deviate. Note this is a WORKAROUND for the missing artifact carrier, not a substitute: it works only because these artifacts belong in git anyway. A brief attachment that is not a repo file still has no carrier — that is #79, and the improvement issue stands.

deviations.what: Wave-0 round 2 blocked on sandbox posture: under codex --sandbox workspace-write the WORKTREE is writable but .git is READ-ONLY, so git fetch/commit/branch all fail ('.git/FETCH_HEAD: Read-only file system'). Both P2 (run 01M023GXENMQ0QRZQH5G61TXD9) and P3 (run 01M023GXJB2ARP1B8213Q992AT) reported it independently after their write probes passed. Packages must be re-dispatched with a sandbox that permits git metadata writes, per the agent checkout's own AGENTS.md guidance (danger-full-access).
deviations.reason: This refines #18 rather than reopening it: file writes in the worktree ARE proven (three independent probes), but git-metadata writes are not permitted under workspace-write. The consequence reaches the spec, not just the fan-out: the git_ref handover carrier decided in q9/c70 requires the producing agent to create a commit and a ref, which is exactly what this sandbox forbids. So the two-carrier decision currently depends on either raising the sandbox to danger-full-access for any package that hands over a ref, or on the operator creating the ref on the agent's behalf — which reintroduces the human-as-transport the batch exists to remove. Classified RISKY because raising the sandbox weakens the confinement that made read-only dispatch safe, and that trade deserves an explicit decision rather than being absorbed as a dispatch flag.
